transcript.text: Good morning, everyone. As you know, Paint Booth 4 was stopped this morning after solvent was found pooled beneath its circulation manifold. The booth is currently isolated and cordoned off. I'm the one who makes the final decision on containment, restart authorization, and the recovery plan, but before we can move toward restart, the incident authorization form needs documented entries for equipment repair, hazardous-waste handling, production recovery, and disposition of potentially contaminated panels. On top of that, restart policy requires findings from maintenance, environmental compliance, production, and quality to be attached to that form before I can finalize authorization. So I need each of those areas to weigh in. Let's start by hearing from maintenance on what caused the solvent pooling and what repairs are needed.
transcript.speaker: A1

transcript.text: My inspection this morning found a cracked manifold isolation valve seat, which is the source of the solvent pooling. Replacing the valve requires exactly 4 hours, and maintenance's lockout worksheet identifies exactly 6 isolation points. I completed the inspection this morning but have not yet attached the worksheet to the incident record. I want to be clear: because the valve seat is cracked, Booth 4 must not be authorized to restart regardless of whether the documentation entries are later completed.
transcript.speaker: A2

transcript.text: I need to share my environmental compliance findings. My measured cleanup estimate is exactly 240 liters of solvent-contaminated liquid. Because this exceeds the plant's hazardous-waste threshold, it requires a licensed hauler and a hazardous-waste manifest. I confirmed the threshold with the waste contractor today, but I have not yet entered the estimate in the waste log. I'll get that logged as part of the hazardous-waste handling documentation for the incident form.
transcript.speaker: A3

transcript.text: I've got production recovery covered. I confirmed that Booth 2 can run exactly 180 affected units per shift on both Wednesday and Thursday, which means we can reroute exactly 360 units from the Booth 4 schedule to Booth 2 without exceeding its approved rate. I received this capacity confirmation from the scheduling desk, but I should note I have not yet revised the production board to reflect this.
transcript.speaker: A4

transcript.text: I need to share my quality findings. This morning I completed wipe sampling and found solvent residue on exactly 36 panels that were staged beside Booth 4. Those 36 panels must remain on quality hold and receive solvent-residue inspection before release. I completed the sampling this morning but have not yet issued the hold tags. I'll get the tags applied and document the disposition of these potentially contaminated panels for the incident authorization form.
transcript.speaker: A5
